# Fixed typed input scope

The manifest pins official shadcn/ui commit `8ab27715521cbd4f87ae6886cd989cbb678f6de7`. Every original is byte-for-byte copied, with its fixed raw URL, SHA-256 and Git blob recorded. Regenerate by reading each `origin`, checking both hashes and byte length, and writing it to the listed `archive` path. No transformed React source is used as a behavioral oracle for native platform internals.

The Base Input wrapper forwards native HTML input properties and unifies appearance. Its actual `InputTypes` collection uses password, telephone, URL, search, number, date, time and file; basic/label/description/disabled examples use email/text. The standalone InputFile associates Picture with a file input and description. The runnable `examples/typed-input` covers these types plus native select, button, Field/InputGroup and form interactions. Existing string Input and its IME, password, search, read-only and error behavior stay intact.

## Native implementation

- `StyleInput` exposes the kit's established appearance for actual native editor roots. Styling a compound SDK root does not give access to private parts.
- `NumberInput` binds a finite `float64` and uses the same public native text/IME editor as Input. A separate editable draft allows incomplete signs/exponents and preserves selection/undo. Finite in-range complete edits update typed state; Enter or blur canonicalizes/reverts to committed state. Up/Down step and clamp by the optional bounds. Step defaults to one and is not browser step-mismatch validation. Invalid ranges or nonpositive/nonfinite steps mark the editor invalid and read-only; nonfinite model values mark it invalid. Both bounds publish public Range/Step metadata on the real text editor. It is a native text field, not an emulation of browser spinbutton buttons, HTML validity bubbles or a localized decimal parser. MyGo's compound NumberInput cannot publicly forward Field labels/errors to its private text editor, which is why this bounded adapter uses TextInputBase instead.
- `DateInput` uses the SDK's localized date button and calendar. The selected `time.Time` preserves clock fields and Location. `TimeInput` uses localized native hour/minute/period segments. Group metadata and segment naming follow the SDK: Field/LabelFor supply the visible label plus native LabelledBy relation, so segments inherit the correct name prefix. Invalid/description/error metadata binds to the group; the SDK exposes no segment parts, per-segment field metadata, read-only mode, segment Handle or segment autofocus. The Time Handle targets the group. InputGroup can style the group, but prefix activation cannot select a private time segment. Native focus highlighting for the internal segments remains owned by the SDK.
- `FileInput` is an accessible native button styled as a file input, backed by `mygo.Dialog.Open`. Only pointer/keyboard activation starts the picker. It runs outside View; only paths/error and weak Services cross back, then current build callbacks apply the result. Cancellation preserves prior selection. Filters and callback paths are cloned. Removing or rebinding the owner invalidates pending results; a single-file picker keeps its first path. Application-owned `FilePicker` injection supports testing/custom native dialog integration; never capture a Context/Element in it. Paths are local native file paths, not browser File/Blob objects.
- Email, telephone and URL use ordinary native string Input. The example's application validates email/URL and shows Field errors. Browser-specific keyboard hints, autofill, web form constraint bubbles and browser File security semantics are not available through this desktop SDK.

`input_typed_test.go` exercises real public UI input: drafts/IME/undo, range stepping, Field and InputGroup target relations, calendar keyboard/cancellation, time segments/date/Location, async picker cancellation/errors/copies and owner unmount/rebinding. Example tests run complete input/form/attachment flows without automatically opening an operating-system dialog. Real platform chooser and assistive technology acceptance are separate platform checks.
